item.title: Five years on, China's youngest stock exchange carves out a niche for small innovators
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- An artificial intelligence (AI) model in training or a complex scientific simulation needs computing power. The less visible challenge is matching each job with suitable computing resources across a nationwide network. Beijing Paratera Tech Corp., Ltd. has built its business around that task. Once a computing job is submitted, its scheduling system matches the workload with suitable resources, while its self-developed platform manages and dynamically allocates computing resources nationwide. The company was still in a phase of rapid expansion and heavy research spending when it listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange, or BSE, on Nov. 1, 2023. It listed under the exchange's second set of standards, centered on market value, revenue growth and operating cash flow, and raised 290 million yuan (about 43 million U.S. dollars) in its IPO. The proceeds have since gone toward core computing-resource scheduling technology and building a nationwide integrated computing network. Paratera fits the profile the BSE was designed to serve: a smaller, innovation-led business seeking public-market capital while scaling its technology and operations. China announced the exchange on Sept. 2, 2021, as part of efforts to support innovation by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), saying it would be built as the primary platform serving innovation-oriented SMEs. Five years later, the exchange has grown from 81 companies at the start of trading to 339. More than 60 percent are national-level "little giant" firms, a designation for specialized and innovative SMEs, and the share among companies newly listed in 2026 is close to 90 percent. Companies in strategic emerging industries and advanced manufacturing account for more than 80 percent of listed companies. The BSE works in tandem with the National Equities Exchange and Quotations, or NEEQ, in a tiered cultivation system for smaller businesses. The NEEQ has served 14,000 SMEs, and nearly 850 companies cultivated through the market have gone on to list in Beijing, Shanghai or Shenzhen. More than 80 percent received funding support while quoted on the NEEQ. Its rules reflect that role. The BSE uses four sets of listing standards that take into account market value, revenue, net profit and R&D investment, accommodating companies at different stages of growth. Over its first five years, it has helped SMEs raise about 80 billion yuan, with more than 80 percent of the funds raised going to green and low-carbon development, the digital economy, high-end equipment manufacturing and new materials. For Hubei Kait Automotive Electronic & Electrical Systems Co., Ltd., or KAIT, a maker of automotive sensors and actuators, that financing model has translated into new products. The company moved from the NEEQ to its Innovation Layer and then to the BSE. In its 2023 IPO, KAIT initially earmarked proceeds mainly for controllers and temperature sensors, but later redirected some funds toward automotive actuators as demand surged amid rapid advances in vehicle intelligence across China's new energy vehicle sector. Its active-grille-shutter actuators have since been installed at scale in new vehicles, expanding the availability of domestically produced alternatives in a segment supplied largely by overseas manufacturers. KAIT has also used equity incentives to attract and retain R&D and management talent and has expanded into areas including data-center liquid cooling and embodied intelligence. The same pattern appears in very different industries. Beijing Tri-Prime Gene Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. has brought a digitalized production facility fully online and is leading a Beijing municipal key laboratory focused on long-acting targeted delivery technologies for peptide and nucleic-acid drugs. Chairman Cheng Yongqing said listing brought changes beyond financing. Ongoing regulatory requirements, he said, had also pushed the company to strengthen corporate governance, information disclosure, internal controls, R&D and branding. Across the exchange, R&D intensity and the number of invention patents are both more than twice the average for enterprises above the designated size in China. Eighteen BSE companies have been recognized as manufacturing "single champions," a designation for manufacturers that lead in specialized market segments, while 17 have received national science and technology awards. Trading activity has grown alongside the market. Average daily turnover has risen from less than 1 billion yuan in the BSE's early days to more than 20 billion yuan so far in 2026, while the number of qualified investors has climbed from about 4 million to more than 11 million. Institutional investors now account for 24 percent of trading, up from 9 percent at the market's launch. International market advisers have also taken note. A midyear review by KPMG, a global organization of independent professional services firms, said the BSE "stood out" in the first half of 2026, with 36 new listings raising 11.4 billion yuan. Both the number of listings and funds raised were five times their year-earlier levels. The BSE also sits within a much larger SME economy. The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said in its 2026 review of SME financing that SMEs contribute roughly 70 percent of China's technological innovation, 60 percent of GDP and 80 percent of urban employment. The report tracks SME equity fundraising on the BSE alongside Shanghai's STAR Market and Shenzhen's ChiNext. China has continued to broaden capital-market channels for innovative companies. Shanghai's STAR Market supports companies in high-tech and strategic emerging sectors, while Shenzhen's ChiNext mainly serves growth-oriented innovative and entrepreneurial companies. Regulators have also expanded listing standards and introduced measures to make refinancing, equity incentives and mergers and acquisitions more flexible. Within that broader system, the BSE focuses on innovative SMEs. It operates with the NEEQ in an integrated, tiered structure, creating a progression from NEEQ cultivation to a BSE listing for qualifying companies. At the larger end of China's technology-financing landscape, 2026 has also brought major listings. Memory-chip maker CXMT Corporation raised about 66.6 billion yuan in gross proceeds in its Shanghai STAR Market offering, making it the largest-ever IPO on the board. Humanoid-robot maker Yushu Technology Co., Ltd., known as Unitree Robotics, raised about 6.1 billion yuan in gross proceeds in its August STAR Market offering. Beyond the public markets, the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026 counted 381 unicorns in China, the world's second-largest total and 38 more than a year earlier. Separately, China ranked first among countries and territories in the Nature Index 2026 Research Leaders, based on 2025 publication data from 178 selected high-quality publications. For Paratera, that wider story comes back to computing power: matching demand with resources across a nationwide network. Five years after the exchange was announced, the task is different but the logic is familiar -- matching a growing group of smaller innovators with public-market capital. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates King Haakon VIII of Norway on accession to throne
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday sent a congratulatory message to Haakon VIII on his accession to the throne as King of Norway. Xi said that although China and Norway are geographically distant, the two countries enjoy a long-standing friendship. Norway was among the first European countries to recognize the People's Republic of China and establish diplomatic relations with it, he said. Over the past 72 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, with the active support and promotion of the Norwegian royal family, bilateral relations have made significant progress, and cooperation in various fields has continued to expand, bringing tangible benefits to the two peoples, Xi said. The Chinese president said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Norway relations and is ready to work with King Haakon VIII to write a new chapter in the friendly exchanges between the two countries. ■

item.title: Xi calls for SCO to strive for higher quality development, promote better global governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
* China is ready to work with all parties to continue to strive for higher quality development, and make the global governance system more just and equitable, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Tuesday during the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the "SCO Plus" meeting. * At the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history, he said. * At the "SCO Plus" meeting, Xi called on the SCO to shoulder the responsibility of the times and work together to advance a more just and equitable global governance system, as well as an equal and orderly multipolar world. BISHKEK, Sept. 1 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Tuesday that China is ready to work with all parties to continue to strive for higher quality development, and make the global governance system more just and equitable. Xi made the remarks in his speeches at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the "SCO Plus" meeting held in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. PUTTING DEVELOPMENT FIRST This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. Xi said that over the past 25 years, the most significant achievement of the organization has been its gradual transformation into a new type of regional cooperation organization that spans the largest geographical area, represents the largest population, and possesses enormous development potential in the world. The SCO's most important experience for cooperation is that it has found the right way of coexistence featuring non-alliances, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, while bringing countries in the region together to build a common home, he added. At the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history, he said. Xi put forward a four-point proposal at the summit, calling on the SCO to stay committed to putting development and the people first, taking security as a key goal, and promoting dialogue and consultation. The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), digital economy, green industry and green mining. China will develop an international AI application cooperation center with fellow SCO countries, establish a China-SCO port economic cooperation center in Tianjin, and implement 100 technological cooperation projects with other SCO countries in the next three years, he said. The SCO should pursue coordinated measures to tackle traditional and non-traditional security threats, Xi said, adding that the organization must prevent external forces from interfering in internal affairs, endangering political security, and undermining regional stability. China stands ready to work with all parties to act on the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and support the early opening of the SCO's four security centers, so as to upgrade the capacity of member states in responding to security threats and challenges, Xi said. According to Alexey Mukhin, director general of the Centre for Political Information in Moscow, the outcomes of the SCO summit demonstrated that all member states are focusing on development and security priorities, and working together to address threats and challenges and promote long-term development through effective mechanisms within the SCO framework. This not only serves the common interests of all parties, but also contributes to improving regional and global governance, Mukhin said. China stands ready to work with all parties to implement the Global Civilization Initiative, Xi said, adding that China will host SCO forums on innovation and sustainable development, on people-to-people friendship and on friendship cities, as well as establish a China-SCO basic education cooperation center. The SCO should always advocate that all countries, regardless of their size, are equal, and that regional affairs should be discussed by all countries to bridge differences and build consensus, properly handle differences through dialogue and consultation, and meet common challenges through multilateral collaboration, Xi said. ADVANCING GLOBAL GOVERNANCE At the "SCO Plus" meeting, Xi called on the SCO to shoulder the responsibility of the times and work together to advance a more just and equitable global governance system, as well as an equal and orderly multipolar world. In his address, Xi noted that the trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible, and multipolarity, independent choice of development paths, and greater democracy in international relations are the right way forward. Xi said that in recent years, the rise of the Global South is driving a profound shift in the international balance of power. As an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs, he said. Xi said that as a responsible major country, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world, in which sovereign equality and mutual respect should be upheld as fundamental principles, balance, order and the rule of law as essential requirements, multipolarism, dialogue and consultation as key pathways, and mutual benefit, win-win cooperation and universally beneficial and inclusive development as the way forward. "Major countries in particular should take the lead in observing international norms and honoring the rule of law, and work together to tackle global challenges," Xi said. China, as a major country, has set an example in this regard and played a leading role, said Seun Sam, a policy analyst at the Royal Academy of Cambodia. "Major countries taking the lead in abiding by international law can have a demonstrative effect, help safeguard the sovereignty and interests of small countries like Cambodia, promote mutual trust among countries, and achieve peaceful coexistence," he said. Xi called on countries to promote the common values of humanity, advance the rule of law in international relations, restore the authority and vitality of the United Nations, and improve the coordination and efficiency of global and regional multilateral mechanisms. "We should focus on the development agenda, uphold openness and cooperation, and bridge the digital and AI divides, so that technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations," Xi said. Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University, said that with its deep experience in multilateral cooperation, the SCO has developed mature practices for transcending differences, building consensus and fostering cooperation. It enables countries with different political systems, cultural traditions and interests to engage in equal dialogue and practical cooperation, precisely what is needed to build a more just and equitable global governance system, Ulmasov said. Highlighting the role of the SCO, Xi put forward three proposals for the organization to advance common prosperity, promote the development and rise of the Global South, and guide the reform and improvement of global governance, to make greater contributions to an equal and orderly multipolar world. As an important pillar of South-South cooperation, the SCO should carry forward the Shanghai Spirit, strengthen and expand the "SCO Plus" partnerships, and jointly speak up for peace, foster synergy for development, build bridges for cooperation, and pave the way for win-win outcomes, Xi said. "Let us take the people-centered and action-oriented approach, jointly advocate an equal and orderly multipolar world, make global governance more just and equitable, and build a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said. ■

item.title: Xi puts forward four-point proposal at SCO Bishkek summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers an important speech during the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) BISHKEK, Sept. 1 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday put forward a four-point proposal at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. In his speech at the summit, Xi said this year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. He pointed out that 25 years ago, safeguarding sovereignty, security and development interests became a shared consensus among countries in the region in the face of the profound lessons of the Cold War, the real threat posed by the "three evil forces," as well as the strong aspirations of people in various countries for peace and development. The SCO thus emerged, and the organization has increasingly demonstrated its strong vitality and dynamism, Xi added. Over the past 25 years, the SCO has gone through an extraordinary journey, Xi said, noting that its most significant achievement has been its gradual transformation into a new type of regional cooperation organization that spans the largest geographical area, represents the largest population, and possesses enormous development potential in the world. The SCO's most valuable spiritual asset is the pioneering proposal and steadfast adherence to the "Shanghai Spirit" of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations and pursuit of common development, he said. The SCO's most important experience for cooperation is that it has found the right way of coexistence featuring non-alliances, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, while bringing countries in the region together to build a common home, he added. Xi said that 25 years on, as profound changes unseen in a century are accelerating, the rivalry is intensifying between dialogue and confrontation, win-win cooperation and zero-sum, and multilateralism and unilateralism, and the shadow of war continues to haunt the world. At the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history, he said. Xi called on the SCO to stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity. The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining. China sees the SCO as a priority area for the high-quality joint construction of the Belt and Road and implementation of the Global Development Initiative, and will continue to host events such as the SCO Digital Economy Forum and the SCO Agricultural Expo, Xi said. China will also establish an international cooperation center on AI applications for SCO countries, set up a China-SCO port economy cooperation center in Tianjin, and jointly implement 100 technological cooperation projects with SCO countries over the next three years, Xi added. Xi urged the SCO to stay committed to taking security as a key goal, and foster an environment of common security. The SCO should coordinate to counter traditional and non-traditional security threats, combat the "three evil forces," transnational organized crime, drug trafficking and telecommunications fraud, strengthen cooperation on information security, bio-security and outer space security, and prevent external forces from interfering in the internal affairs, endangering political security and undermining regional stability, Xi noted. Xi said China stands ready to work with all parties to act on the vision of a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, and build the SCO into an important platform for implementing the Global Security Initiative. China supports the early opening of the SCO's "four security centers" so as to enhance the capacity of member countries to address security threats and challenges, Xi said. Xi also called on the grouping to put people first, and cement the foundation for everlasting friendship. The SCO should take into account the characteristics of each member state's history, culture, social system and development stage, build cooperation networks between legislatures, political parties, schools, think tanks, enterprises and media, promote people-to-people exchanges, and inject vitality into the good-neighborliness and friendship among member states, he said. China is willing to work with all parties to implement the Global Civilization Initiative, and supports a greater role of the SCO Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation Commission and other organizations of friendly people-to-people exchanges, Xi said. The Chinese side will set up a China-SCO basic education cooperation center, and continue to build bridges for exchanges and mutual learning as well as people-to-people connectivity through such programs as Confucius Institutes and Luban Workshops, he added. Xi also urged the SCO to promote dialogue and consultation, and strive for more equitable and orderly governance. He stressed that the SCO should always advocate that all countries, regardless of their size, are equal, and that regional affairs should be discussed by all countries to bridge differences and build consensus. The SCO should properly handle differences through dialogue and consultation, and meet common challenges through multilateral coordination. China supports the SCO in setting an example in cooperation to implement the Global Governance Initiative, Xi said, calling for continued efforts to improve the SCO's operational mechanisms, and enhance the efficiency of its decision-making and execution. More like-minded countries are welcome to become SCO partners to join the effort to improve regional and global governance, he said. Xi stressed that China is ready to work with all parties to continue to uphold the banner of the "Shanghai Spirit," implement the SCO's development strategy for the next decade, strive for higher quality development, and make greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity. Leaders of member states fully affirmed the achievements the SCO has made in the past 25 years, and recognized that the SCO has provided important guarantee for regional security and prosperity and has become one of the cornerstones of global stability and economic development. All parties expressed appreciation for China's important contribution to the organization's development as a founding member, and agreed to actively implement the strategic vision set out at the 2025 Tianjin summit, continue to uphold the Shanghai Spirit, promote institution-building, enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas including trade, investment, science and technology, energy, finance, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity, strengthen people-to-people bonds, jointly respond to new types of security challenges, with a view to writing a new chapter of lasting peace and common development. In the face of a complex and volatile international situation, SCO member states should embrace solidarity and cooperation, enhance the influence of SCO, promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system, and play a greater role in safeguarding peace, stability and prosperity in the region and beyond. Leaders of the member states signed and issued the Bishkek Declaration, approved the protocol on amendments and additions to the SCO Charter, the regulations on the SCO Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats and the regulations on the SCO Anti-drug Center, and adopted 28 outcome documents covering such areas as security, economic and people-to-people cooperation, and organizational development. The meeting decided that Pakistan will assume the rotating presidency of the SCO for 2026-2027. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping shakes hands with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. item.title: Xi calls on SCO to work toward more just, equitable global governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers an important speech during the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) BISHKEK, Sept. 1 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday called on the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) to shoulder the responsibility of the times and work together to advance a more just and equitable global governance. Xi made the remarks in his speech at the "SCO Plus" meeting in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. "The meeting today focuses on strengthening the role of the United Nations and building a multipolar world, and it demonstrates SCO's commitment to reforming and improving global governance as required by our times," Xi said. "Currently, major changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the globe. Hegemonism, unilateralism and protectionism are resurging against historical trends. Nevertheless, the overwhelming majority of the world do not condone power politics, conflict and confrontation, or isolation and backwardness," he added. What they want instead, Xi said, is to hold a place on the world stage through national development and international cooperation. Xi noted that in recent years, the rise of the Global South is driving a profound shift in the international balance of power, adding that the trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible. "What kind of multipolarity does the world need? How are countries going to take part in and promote it? The international community should build consensus and make the right choice that can stand the test of practice and history," Xi said. Noting that as a responsible major country, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world, Xi said sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles; balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements; multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways; mutual benefit, win-win and inclusiveness are the way forward for development. "We should ensure equal rights, equal opportunities and equal rules for all countries, regardless of their size, strength and wealth," Xi said, adding that "as an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs." He called on various parties to promote the common values of humanity, reject double standards, exceptionalism, foreign interference, bullying and the law of the jungle, and advance the rule of law in international relations. "Major countries in particular should take the lead in observing international norms and honoring the rule of law, and work together to tackle global challenges," he added. Xi also said that world affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all. "The authority and vitality of the United Nations need to be restored. Multilateral mechanisms, global and regional, should enhance their coordination and improve their efficiency," he said. "We should focus on the development agenda, uphold openness and cooperation, and bridge the digital and AI divides, so that technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations," Xi added. Xi noted that after a 25-year journey, the SCO has successfully set a stellar example in conducting relations among big countries, among neighbors, and among countries of different sizes. The SCO, Xi said, has successfully brought together half of the world's population and a quarter of the global economy, generating strong driving forces for development, adding that a more united and vibrant SCO is fully capable of making greater contributions to a multipolar world. "It is important that SCO member states and partners ride the trend of history and shoulder the responsibility of our times. Let us take the people-centered and action-oriented approach, jointly advocate an equal and orderly multipolar world, make global governance more just and equitable, and build a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said. To further enhance the SCO's role, Xi called for advancing common prosperity in the vast continent straddling Asia and Europe with the SCO Strength. "We should continue to leverage our strengths, unlock our potential, and connect the multiple growth poles across the continent through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. We should empower each other, help each other succeed, and work together to create new opportunities and promote shared prosperity," Xi said. "We should promote the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom," Xi said, calling on various parties to "carry forward the Shanghai Spirit, strengthen and expand the SCO Plus partnerships, and jointly speak up for peace, foster synergy for development, build bridges for cooperation, and pave the way for win-win outcomes." Xi also proposed that the SCO countries should guide the reform and improvement of global governance through the SCO Action. "We should stay committed to building partnerships rather than alliances, and engaging in dialogue rather than confrontation," he said. Xi also called for sticking to the principle of "planning together, building together and benefiting together" to encourage equal participation in global governance by all countries and ensure all will benefit from it. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a group photo session during a welcome banquet held by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov ahead of the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. Xi attended the "SCO Plus" meeting and delivered an important speech here on Tuesday. (Xinhua/Wang Ye)
